record.paper_title: Some open problems in dynamical systems
record.original_question: For the same quadratic polynomial family P_α(z) = e^{2πiα} z + z^2 with α a Bruno number and S_α the corresponding Siegel singular disk, does there exist a Bruno number α such that the boundary ∂S_α is not a Jordan curve?

evidence.quote: 2. Does there exist α2 a Bruno number such that ∂Sα2 (the boundary of Sα2 ) is not a Jordan curve ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the quadratic polynomial family
$$P_\alpha(z) = e^{2\pi i \alpha} z + z^2, \qquad z \in \mathbb{C},$$
where $\alpha \in \mathbb{R}\setminus\mathbb{Q}$. Recall that an irrational number $\alpha$ with continued fraction convergents $p_n/q_n$ is called a Brjuno (Bruno) number if
$$\sum_{n=0}^{\infty} \frac{\log q_{n+1}}{q_n} < \infty.$$
By a theorem of Brjuno–Yoccoz, for every Brjuno number $\alpha$ the polynomial $P_\alpha$ is locally linearizable at the fixed point $0$; that is, there is a maximal open neighborhood $S_\alpha$ of $0$ (the Siegel disk of $P_\alpha$) on which $P_\alpha$ is conformally conjugate to the rigid rotation $z \mapsto e^{2\pi i \alpha} z$.

Question: Does there exist a Brjuno number $\alpha$ such that the boundary $\partial S_\alpha$ of the Siegel disk of $P_\alpha$ is not a Jordan curve (i.e., is not homeomorphic to a circle)?
artifact.status_search_result: The general question of whether Siegel disk boundaries of quadratic polynomials with Brjuno rotation number are Jordan curves remains an open problem in complex dynamics. Significant partial results exist: for quadratic polynomials with rotation number of sufficiently high type the Siegel disk is known to be a Jordan domain (Yang, 2016), and for almost all (in a measure-theoretic sense) rotation numbers the boundary is a Jordan curve equal to the closure of the critical orbit. However, no Brjuno parameter has been exhibited for which $\partial S_\alpha$ fails to be a Jordan curve, nor is such non-existence proved in general.

status_evidence.title: Siegel disks/Obstructions - Scholarpedia
status_evidence.snippet: A question asked by Douady and Sullivan about whether Siegel disk boundaries are always Jordan curves remains open, even for quadratic polynomials.
status_evidence.claim: The general Jordan-curve question for Siegel disk boundaries is still open.

status_evidence.title: The high type quadratic Siegel disks are Jordan domains
status_evidence.snippet: For quadratic polynomials with rotation number of sufficiently high type, the boundary of the Siegel disk is a Jordan curve.
status_evidence.claim: Partial result: high-type quadratic Siegel disks have Jordan boundaries.

status_evidence.title: Polynomial Siegel disks are typically Jordan domains
status_evidence.snippet: For almost all rotation numbers the boundary of the Siegel disk is a Jordan curve equal to the closure of the critical orbit.
status_evidence.claim: Generic/typical Brjuno parameters give Jordan-curve boundaries.
